cards.text: King David has just divided the Levites into divisions by the sons of Levi (1 Chronicles 23:6). Now it's the priests' turn, the descendants of Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 6:20). Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Then the family gets smaller. Nadab and Abihu died before their father did.

cards.question: Nadab and Abihu, who died before their father Aaron, left sons behind to serve as priests.

cards.text: So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests. King David divides up their families, with help from Zadok, a descendant of Eleazar, and Ahimelech, a descendant of Ithamar.

cards.question: David, Zadok and Ahimelech split Aaron's descendants into groups. What do they split them by?

cards.text: Then they count the family leaders on each side, and Eleazar's side has MORE. Friend, that's not a split, that's a blowout.

cards.question: Eleazar's line has sixteen heads of families, and Ithamar's line has ___.
The families of Eleazar and Ithamar need an order for serving. How do they decide it?

answers.text: By letting the oldest go first

cards.question: Eleazar's side is twice as big, but both sides go into the same drawing of lots. Why?

answers.text: Both sides had officers of the sanctuary
Ithamar's side asked to be included
The king wanted to honor Ithamar

cards.text: Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite, is the scribe, and he writes down every name. I spent years in a junk drawer under receipts nobody would ever need, so believe me, friend, I know the difference: THESE papers matter.

cards.question: Shemaiah the scribe records the priests' names in front of the ___ and the officers.
As Shemaiah records the names, all of Eleazar's families are taken first, and then all of Ithamar's.

cards.text: Then the lots fall, one family at a time: the first to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah, and all the way down to Maaziah at twenty-fourth. Twenty-four families, twenty-four turns. Nobody gets skipped, and NOBODY cuts the line.

cards.question: The twenty-four families now have their order for serving in the house of the LORD. It follows regulations set by one of their ancestors. Who?
The regulations Aaron set for the priests followed what the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.

cards.text: Next comes a list of the rest of Levi's descendants, family by family, through the lines of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, Uzziel and Merari. One name sticks out: from Mahli comes Eleazar (not Aaron's son Eleazar), who had no sons.

cards.question: These other Levite families stand before King David, Zadok and Ahimelech too. What do they do there?

answers.text: They cast lots like the priests
They let the king choose for them
They let the scribe pick for them

cards.question: When the Levite families cast lots, the family heads got to go ahead of their younger brothers.
